blocks.orig: The Serengeti is renowned for the Great Wildebeest Migration, one of the world’s largest wildlife migrations. It is also one of the few places in Africa where game viewing is spectacular year round. Predator numbers are high, and the Big Five is present as well. The Serengeti is a massive park that spans around 30,000 km2 (12,000 sq miles). So to get the most out of your visit, it is important to plan your safari well. Where you should go in the Serengeti depends largely on what time (season) you choose to visit this beautiful park.
blocks.html: The Serengeti is best known for the Great Wildebeest Migration, among the largest wildlife migrations anywhere in the world. It is also one of the few places in Africa where game viewing is excellent all year round, with high predator numbers and the Big Five present too. The park is huge, covering roughly 30,000 km2 (12,000 sq miles), so careful planning makes a real difference to what you get out of your visit. Which part of the Serengeti you should head for depends mostly on the time of year (the season) you pick for your trip.

blocks.orig: This area is rich in wildlife throughout the year because of the many river valleys. You can see an abundance of lions, leopards, elephants and many more. The Wildebeest Migration head for this part of the Serengeti from April till June and comes back in October, November and December. If the wildebeest migration is the main reason you visit the Serengeti, it’s important to be in the central part during these times. Our travel consultants can tell you more about the exact timing of the wildebeest migration and the best accommodation to stay. Since there is so much to see in this region, we recommend staying here at least one or two days.
blocks.html: Thanks to its many river valleys, this area holds plenty of wildlife in every season. Lions, leopards, elephants and much more can be seen in large numbers. The Wildebeest Migration moves into this section of the Serengeti from April till June and returns in October, November and December. If seeing the migration is the main reason for your Serengeti trip, make sure you are in the central part during those months. Our travel consultants can advise you on the precise timing of the wildebeest migration and on the best places to stay. There is so much to see in this region that we suggest spending at least one or two days here.

blocks.orig: From December till March, these nutrient rich plains are home to the great wildebeest migration during the green season. In February, half a million calves are born on these southern plains. You can see hundred thousand of wildebeest and zebras. But also lots of predators, who are all waiting for the change to eat the placentas of the young calves. Because of all the placentas on the plain. The young calves are relatively safe. The calving season is an amazing spectacle that takes your breath away. We advise you to take your time and spend 2 days in the Ndutu Area at this time. Another option is to spend one day in South Serengeti, since it’s very common to enter the Serengeti from the south. Realize that the schedule will be tight if you only stay one day.
blocks.html: Between December and March, during the green season, the great wildebeest migration gathers on these nutrient rich plains. In February, half a million calves are born in the south. You will see hundreds of thousands of wildebeest and zebras, and plenty of predators as well, all waiting for their chance to feed on the placentas of the newborn calves. With so many placentas lying on the plain, the young calves themselves are relatively safe. Calving season is a remarkable spectacle that will leave you speechless. Our advice is to take it slowly and spend 2 days in the Ndutu Area at this time of year. Alternatively, you could spend one day in South Serengeti, as many travellers enter the park from the south. Be aware that a single day makes for a tight schedule.

blocks.orig: The northern part of the Serengeti is the place to be from July to October, when de migration resides here. You can find the herds around the Mara River and witness the epic river crossings. The sights are impressive as well as dramatic around this time. The fast flowing water and crocodiles make this crossing extremely dangerous for the herds. This northern part of the Serengeti is beautifully remote and quiet, due to the fact that it is about 4-hour drive from the central part. So if you visit this part you will also need accommodation here. We recommend staying at least 2 days in the north to increase the chance of seeing the herds cross the river. It will also give you time to enjoy encounters with other wildlife.
blocks.html: From July to October the migration settles in the northern Serengeti, so that is where you want to be. The herds gather near the Mara River, and you can watch the dramatic river crossings. What you see here at this time is both impressive and tense: the fast flowing water and the crocodiles make every crossing extremely dangerous for the animals. The north of the Serengeti is wonderfully remote and quiet, which is partly because it lies about a 4-hour drive from the central part. If you come here, you will therefore need accommodation in the north as well. We suggest staying at least 2 days to improve your chances of seeing the herds cross the river, and that also leaves you time to enjoy the other wildlife.
